newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end week at record high.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end week at record high.

text.p: Australian shares capped a strong week with a record close on Friday, the market healthy enough to absorb profit-taking on News Corp and bank stocks which posted strong gains on Thursday.
Key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index, set its second record closing high in a row and its third for the week, ending 17.2 points firmer at 2,655.3.
The June share price index finished 10 points up at 2,663, a 7.7 point premium to the underlying index.
Food group Burns Philp led turnover after a mystery buyer snared 14.7 percent of its shares before the opening bell.

Burns Philp finished the day 40 cents higher at A$2.43 (US$1.82) after brokerage Deutsche Morgan Grenfell confirmed it had acted for one party when it bought 78.16 million shares at a price of A$2.50.
The shares of Australia and New Zealand Banking Group drifted 13.2 cents to A$9.65, as speculation eased that the bank was soon to be the target of a foreign bid.
Media group News Corp also fell prey to profit-takers, its ordinary shares closing 13 cents lower at A$6.14.
The stock gained 40 cents on Thursday after News announced a deal to sell its U.S. satellite TV interests and pay cash rather than shares for a children's cable TV network.
Diversified manufacturer Pacific Dunlop was another active stock, closing the session with a gain of 10 cents at A$3.68 on turnover of 11.3 million shares.
Dealers could not point to any news driving the stock but said its cyclical nature made it a favourite after a good night on Wall Street.
Resources outperformed industrials with market heavyweights, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and Rio Tinto, both finishing the week with solid gains.
Amongst the industrials, two outstanding performers were Brambles Industries and Westpac Banking Group.

Transport group Brambles closed 98.2 cents higher at A$25.40 while dealers said Westpac, which finished 38.7 cents higher at A$7.75, benefited from the takeover speculation left over from ANZ's run on Thursday.
"There seemed to be a shortage of stock at the end of the day particularly for BHP and bank issues," said Grant Williams, a dealer at Sydney brokerage, Reynolds and Co.
Williams said the market was reasonably confident Wall Street would continue to run higher next week although Australian investors were wary about the strength of the Dow's rally in the past month.
